root_cause.text: In `nilfs_ioctl_mark_blocks_dirty()` in NILFS2, the code used `bd_oblocknr` as the “dead block” validity check, but failed to reject a zero `bd_oblocknr`, allowing a crafted ioctl descriptor to bypass the dead-block test when `nilfs_bmap_lookup_at_level()` returned `-ENOENT` and set `bd_blocknr` to 0.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an explicit `if (unlikely(!bdescs[i].bd_oblocknr)) return -EINVAL;` with the comment that “bd_oblocknr must never be 0 as block 0 is never a valid GC target block,” and the CVE description says a corrupted ioctl request with `bd_oblocknr = 0` makes the comparison incorrectly match, bypassing the dead block check and leading to `nilfs_btree_do_lookup()` returning `-ENOENT` and triggering `WARN_ON(ret == -ENOENT)`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds an explicit `if (unlikely(!bdescs[i].bd_oblocknr)) return -EINVAL;` with the comment that “bd_oblocknr must never be 0 as block 0 is never a valid GC target block,” and the CVE description says a corrupted ioctl request with `bd_oblocknr = 0` makes the comparison incorrectly match, bypassing the dead block check and leading to `nilfs_btree_do_lookup()` returning `-ENOENT` and triggering `WARN_ON(ret == -ENOENT)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early validity check to reject block descriptors with object block number 0 in NILFS dirty-block marking.
intent_record.what: A validation check was added at the start of the loop in nilfs_ioctl_mark_blocks_dirty(): before processing each block descriptor, the code now returns -EINVAL if bdescs[i].bd_oblocknr is zero, with a comment noting that block 0 is not a valid GC target block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the ioctl will now reject requests that include a zero object block number instead of continuing into block lookup and dirty-marking logic. This prevents invalid block 0 entries from being processed as garbage-collection targets and causes the operation to fail early with an error.

grouping_result.intent: Add an early validity check to reject block descriptors with object block number 0 in NILFS dirty-block marking.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an early check to reject block descriptors with object block number 0, which prevents the crafted ioctl descriptor from bypassing the dead-block validation when lookup returns -ENOENT and sets the block number to 0.

candidates.rationale: This lookup is the point where the code can return -ENOENT and leave the block descriptor with bd_blocknr set to 0, which then should have been rejected. The vulnerability stems from failing to add a zero-check after this operation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This lookup can return -ENOENT and leave the block descriptor with bd_blocknr set to 0; the missing post-lookup zero-value rejection allowed the dead-block validity check to be bypassed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `nilfs_ioctl_do_mark_blocks_dirty()`. The code does `ret = nilfs_bmap_lookup_at_level(..., &bdescs[i].bd_blocknr);` and on `-ENOENT` explicitly sets `bdescs[i].bd_blocknr = 0;`. It then checks `if (bdescs[i].bd_blocknr != bdescs[i].bd_oblocknr) /* skip dead block */ continue;`. There is no explicit rejection of a zero `bd_oblocknr`, so a crafted descriptor with `bd_oblocknr == 0` can satisfy this equality when lookup returns `-ENOENT` and sets `bd_blocknr` to 0. The fix is not present here because there is no additional `bd_oblocknr != 0` validation or equivalent guard.
